clue.text: One of Hillary's friends in high places?

definitions.text: One of Hillary's friends in high places?

parts.words: One of Hillary's friends in high places
parts.note: Edmund Hillary climbed Everest with Himalayan mountain guides, companions who were literally high up

explanation.surface: A political insider close to a famous Hillary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a well-connected ally of a politician called Hillary; the Hillary meant is the mountaineer, and the high places are Himalayan peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Nepalese people served as guides and porters on Himalayan expeditions, including Tenzing Norgay with Hillary in 1953.

clue.text: Surface to air missile

parts.note: a projectile scooped from the ground's covering in winter and hurled through the air

explanation.surface: A military rocket launched from the ground at aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: A surface-to-air missile sounds like military hardware, but here the surface is snowy ground and the missile is thrown by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed ball of winter precipitation is gathered from the ground and thrown through the air at a target.

clue.text: One will improve our delivery style, using the spare pitches

indicators.note: the letters of the spare pitches are given a new style, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A coach improving a bowler's delivery by using the practice pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' and 'pitches' suggest cricket bowling; the delivery is speech, and 'style' rearranges THE SPARE PITCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist treats problems with spoken communication, improving how a person delivers words.

clue.text: It is put into orbit to improve the outlook

definitions.text: It is put into orbit to improve the outlook

parts.words: It is put into orbit to improve the outlook
parts.note: orbit here is the eye socket, and the outlook is one's eyesight; a small cup is held against it to rinse it

explanation.surface: A satellite launched to improve forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbit' suggests space launches, but an orbit is also the bony socket of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup shaped to fit the eye socket is used to rinse the eye, helping the wearer see.

clue.text: Taking all foul material away from comedian, no taint is the result

indicators.note: the letters of comedian and no taint, rearranged, produce what results

explanation.surface: A clean comedian whose act removes all smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the result' signals that COMEDIAN and NO TAINT are rearranged; the surface picture of a clean comic hides this.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing something of pollutants, poisons or radioactive matter removes every harmful substance from it.

clue.text: Set, for example, can be a shock before a party

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a shock is a thick bushy mass of hair
a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A fright just before a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle such as a shampoo and set is an arrangement made by a hairdresser.

clue.text: Grounds of general leading the south

indicators.note: the general's name goes in front of the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
S is the standard abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A general commanding the Confederate South.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert E. Lee led the Southern army in the American Civil War, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment that settles at the bottom of wine or coffee is also called its dregs.

clue.text: On what occasion is this enough for a drinker?

definitions.meaning: a question asking at what time something happens

definitions.text: is this enough for a drinker?
definitions.meaning: someone pouring a drink says 'say ...' so the drinker can call a halt

explanation.definitionFit: The word asks at what time, and is also what a drinker says to stop the pour, as in 'say when'.

clue.text: Carry on in the Strand, say?

definitions.meaning: to carry on a trade is to work at it steadily
a strand is a single thickness of yarn or rope; the capital S disguises a common noun

explanation.definitionFit: To work steadily at a trade is a verb sense; a layer or twisted thread of wool or rope is the noun sense.

clue.text: English label left in coat

parts.note: a name is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: An English brand label sewn into a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy layer of paint or glaze applied over a surface is a protective covering.

clue.text: Hardly a good read-bad at first with worse, perhaps, to follow

indicators.note: the reworked letters come after the first piece
only the opening letter of the word bad is used
worse is a possible arrangement of its own letters, which are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A book review: bad to begin with and worse afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WORSE into ROWSE, which follows B.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim casually through a book rather than study it is hardly a thorough read.

clue.text: It gives volume control

parts.note: volume here is a book, and this stand holds it steady and open for the reader

explanation.surface: A knob on a stereo that adjusts loudness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume control' suggests sound; the volume is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand that props an open book at an angle keeps the pages under control while reading.

clue.text: These army jumpers ride up!

parts.note: army jumpers sounds like military sweaters, but these soldiers jump from aircraft and their canopies ride up as they open

explanation.surface: Military-issue sweaters that ride up the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' are British sweaters, and a jumper that rides up is badly fitting; here the jumpers are soldiers who leap from planes.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne soldiers who leap from aircraft and descend under canopies are army jumpers.

clue.text: This old bird is dappled, except for the tail

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: pied means patched or dappled in two colours

explanation.surface: An old bird with dappled plumage apart from its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: PIED loses its last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the magpie, a black-and-white bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Hotspur's leaders score first-there's a cry from the field

indicators.note: the score is to come first in the answer, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a tally is a score or count

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word Hotspur's are taken

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur's leaders score early, and a cheer goes up from the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club, so 'score' and 'field' suggest football. The leaders here are H and O, the first two letters of Hotspur's.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntsman's shout on sighting the fox is called out across the fields during a hunt.

clue.text: Bitter in hospital experiment?

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words hospital experiment

explanation.surface: A bitter outcome of a hospital trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like an adjective but is a kind of beer, British bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a type of beer, a well-hopped British pale brew.

clue.text: Conceal her most secret design

indicators.note: the letters of her most are given a new hidden pattern, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Hiding a woman's most private plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secret design' rearranges HER MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover something so completely that it is suppressed or hidden is to stifle it.

clue.text: Pine, in trial, makes a light, but useful, box

indicators.note: the word for pining sits inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
to pine is to long or ache for something

explanation.surface: Pine wood under testing produces a light but handy box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' suggests timber, apt for a box, but it is the verb meaning yearn, ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light wooden crate originally for shipping leaves is often reused for storage or moving house.

clue.text: A chum takes half an hour to be a dabbler

parts.note: a mate is a chum or friend

indicators.note: the second half of the word hour is used

explanation.surface: A friend who spends half an hour dabbling at a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the pieces; the half used is the last half of HOUR, UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pursues an activity for pleasure, not as a profession, merely dabbles in it.

clue.text: Emulsion paint chaps mark capriciously?

parts.note: tempera is paint made with an emulsion such as egg yolk
men are chaps
a tally is a mark scored for counting

explanation.surface: Decorators splashing emulsion and marking walls erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emulsion paint' suggests household paint, but it is the artists' egg-based TEMPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving moodily and unpredictably, in line with a volatile nature, is acting capriciously.

clue.text: Collect, say, in such a service?

definitions.text: Collect, say, in such a service?

parts.words: Collect, say, in such a service
parts.note: to collect someone by car is to fetch them, and a service that does this is named after that action

explanation.surface: A collection service picking up goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather or fetch someone or something is to collect it, and a collection service bears the same name.

clue.text: Refuse the family

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun means rubbish or waste scattered about
a group of young animals born to one mother at one time

explanation.definitionFit: Scattered rubbish is one sense; a brood of puppies or kittens born together is another.

clue.text: Right out of town near Manchester, comes a container holding bones

indicators.note: the letter for right is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Stockport is a town just south of Manchester

explanation.surface: Leaving a town near Manchester with a box of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT, a town in Greater Manchester, loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cooking vessel in which bones simmer to make broth holds them while the stock cooks.

clue.text: Soldiers on ship (News Agency)

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Soldiers aboard a ship, as reported by a press agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union's official wire service distributed state news reports worldwide.

clue.text: Bligh's call a success in it, coming back

indicators.note: the success goes inside the turned word
the word it is read backwards

parts.note: the word it is used as written
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: Captain Bligh shouting about a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns IT into TI, and A HIT goes inside it. Captain Bligh's HMS Bounty called at this island before the famous mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific island was the Bounty's port of call to collect breadfruit plants.

clue.text: Problems in magazines

definitions.meaning: matters in dispute or difficulties to resolve
editions of a periodical published at intervals

explanation.definitionFit: Points of difficulty are one sense; individual numbers of a periodical are another.

clue.text: Some of Ursa Minor's debris returns to be seen from Earth by only a few

definitions.text: to be seen from Earth by only a few

indicators.note: the picked letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Fragments of the Little Bear constellation fall back, glimpsed from Earth by few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes OFU from 'of Ursa', and 'returns' reverses it; 'Minor's debris' is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mysterious flying craft claimed to be sighted by a handful of observers is rarely seen by most people.

clue.text: But in Slough, we hear

definitions.meaning: a small hut or outbuilding for storing tools
slough pronounced 'sluff' rather than like the town means to cast off skin

explanation.definitionFit: A garden outbuilding is one sense; a snake casting its skin is the other, said with the 'sluff' pronunciation.
